## Document

A document as a record: the artefact plus who owns it, which version it is, and what it replaced. Fields: `title`, `kind` (policy / procedure / record / evidence / report / other), `file` linked to a **FileDef**, `info` (reusing base's Document Info metadata block), `version`, `owner`, `supersedes`, `tags`, and the `contentHash` / `hashedAt` pair.

```ts
import { Document } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/audit/document';
@field document = linksTo(() => Document);
```

The file is a `linksTo(FileDef)` rather than bytes on the card, so the platform's file shells do the previewing and every file family the base supports works here on arrival.

**`supersedes` is why this is a card and not a field.** Evidence is replaced, never deleted: a superseded document stays readable from every finding that cited it, which is only possible while it keeps its own identity and URL. The chain is one link per version, walked backwards.

`contentHash` is a fact about the artefact; the tamper comparison lives on Proof Field, which records the hash it saw when the evidence was attached.

## Examples
Two linked examples: v2 carries a SHA-256 and supersedes v1. **Neither links its file**: a realm file is served as `file-meta` but not indexed, so a `linksTo(FileDef)` to it reads as broken. Both examples therefore show the no-file state, with the hash recorded.

## Non-goals
Not a file (that is FileDef, and this links one). No approval or signature workflow — a document that needs signing is contract paper; see the Contract kit. No full-text search or extraction beyond the base metadata block. Promotes the near-empty `experiments-realm/crm/document.gts` stub, which had only a computed title.
